name: The New York Times Company
moat_justification: Brand trust plus the multi-product bundle (News, Games, Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic) creates real habit and switching friction at 13.35M subscribers, with proven price step-ups; but ROIC is mid-teens (10.8% in 2022 to 18.4% in 2025), not wide-moat through a cycle, and discovery is hostage to search/AI platforms.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 2.89 vs 3-yr median 1.89 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.6%) vs bull-case tier C (12.4%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: High-quality debt-free subscription compounder, moat 6/10 — but at $67.78 the weighted IRR is only 10.2% (IV@15% $39.73); it does not clear 15% until ~$40, and the bear-to-bull band (D to C) says size to the bear end.
moat_for: Scarce trusted news brand; the bundle (News + Games + Cooking + Wirecutter + Athletic) builds daily habit and lowers churn
Direct paid relationship at scale: 13.35M total subscribers, 12.80M digital-only (Q2 2026)
Proven pricing power: digital-only ARPU $9.94, +3.1% YoY in Q2 2026, on promo step-ups and tenured price increases
Journalism cost spread over millions of subscribers; operating margin expanded 8.7% (2022) to 15.3% (2025) to 16.0% TTM
moat_against: AI answers and search-referral erosion threaten discovery; platform dependence for new-subscriber funnel
News is partially substitutable and attention competition is intense; US subscriber pool eventually saturates and bundle adds dilute ARPU
Print is in structural decline and legacy costs remain a drag
Content and video investment keeps adjusted costs growing 8-9%; OpenAI/Microsoft litigation is expensive and a fair-use loss would weaken AI licensing leverage
